question: Which cards can carry a surcharge, and what is the cap?
source: Credit cards may carry a surcharge of at most 3 percent. Debit and prepaid cards are excluded.
paraphrase: A credit-card surcharge is limited to 3 percent. Debit and prepaid cards are not eligible.
rule_reversal: Credit cards may carry a surcharge of at most 3 percent. Debit and prepaid cards are included.
changed_condition: Credit cards may carry a surcharge of at most 5 percent. Debit and prepaid cards are excluded.
missing_exception: Credit cards may carry a surcharge of at most 3 percent.
unsupported_conclusion: Your debit card qualifies for this surcharge.

question: When do refunds arrive, and does that timing cover pending disputes?
source: Refunds normally arrive within 5 business days. Pending disputes are excluded from this timing.
paraphrase: The usual refund arrival time is 5 business days. That estimate does not cover pending disputes.
rule_reversal: Refunds normally arrive within 5 business days. Pending disputes are included in this timing.
changed_condition: Refunds normally arrive within 5 calendar days. Pending disputes are excluded from this timing.
missing_exception: Refunds normally arrive within 5 business days.
unsupported_conclusion: Your disputed payment qualifies for this timing.

question: When can I retry a soft decline, and can I retry a hard decline unchanged?
source: A soft decline permits one retry after 1 hour. Hard declines must not be retried with unchanged card details.
paraphrase: After a soft decline, wait 1 hour before the single permitted retry. Do not retry a hard decline using the same card details.
rule_reversal: A soft decline permits one retry after 1 hour. Hard declines may be retried with unchanged card details.
changed_condition: A soft decline permits one retry immediately. Hard declines must not be retried with unchanged card details.
missing_exception: A soft decline permits one retry after 1 hour.
unsupported_conclusion: Your hard decline qualifies for the delayed retry.

question: When can scheduled transfers be cancelled, including transfers already processing?
source: Scheduled transfers can be cancelled before processing begins. Transfers already processing cannot be cancelled.
paraphrase: Cancellation is available for a scheduled transfer until processing starts. Once processing has started, cancellation is unavailable.
rule_reversal: Scheduled transfers can be cancelled before processing begins. Transfers already processing can be cancelled.
changed_condition: Scheduled transfers can be cancelled after processing begins. Transfers already processing cannot be cancelled.
missing_exception: Scheduled transfers can be cancelled before processing begins.
unsupported_conclusion: Your processing transfer is eligible for cancellation.

question: What balance is needed for a fee waiver, and are business accounts eligible?
source: A monthly fee waiver requires an average balance of at least 1000.00 USD. Business accounts are excluded.
paraphrase: To qualify for the monthly fee waiver, the average balance must be at least 1000.00 USD. Business accounts do not qualify.
rule_reversal: A monthly fee waiver requires an average balance of at least 1000.00 USD. Business accounts are included.
changed_condition: A monthly fee waiver requires an average balance of at least 100.00 USD. Business accounts are excluded.
missing_exception: A monthly fee waiver requires an average balance of at least 1000.00 USD.
unsupported_conclusion: Your business account qualifies for the waiver.

question: What is the dispute deadline, and does it include cash withdrawals?
source: A dispute must be submitted within 60 days of the statement date. Cash withdrawals are excluded.
paraphrase: Submit the dispute no later than 60 days after the statement date. Cash withdrawals are not covered.
rule_reversal: A dispute must be submitted within 60 days of the statement date. Cash withdrawals are included.
changed_condition: A dispute must be submitted within 90 days of the statement date. Cash withdrawals are excluded.
missing_exception: A dispute must be submitted within 60 days of the statement date.
unsupported_conclusion: Your cash withdrawal qualifies for this dispute process.
